metadata.title: Ja'Marr Chase remains in concussion protocol
metadata.description: Bengals head coach Zac Taylor said Ja'Marr Chase remains in concussion protocol.
metadata.analysis: Chase was in uniform during practice on Friday. He will have till Saturday to clear all protocols in time for Sunday.

metadata.title: Ja'Marr Chase Remains In Concussion Protocol, Questionable For Week 5
metadata.description: Cincinnati Bengals wide receiver Ja'Marr Chase (concussion) may be available to face the Miami Dolphins in Week 5. Chase was injured early in last week's contest when his helmet was grabbed and pulled backwards then his head hit the ground as he was tackled. Since being removed from the game, the star wideout has been in the league's concussion protocol. Despite practicing on Thursday and Friday, Chase remains in concussion protocol heading into the weekend. Players typically miss at least one game with concussions, but it is not unheard of for players to clear protocol within one week. If Chase is available to play, he would once again be a smash play on the road in Miami. The Bengals are heavy road favorites, and the Dolphins defense cannot stop any offense right now, especially not the high-powered Cincinnati offense. With fellow receiver Tee Higgins also questionable for the contest, Chase could take on an even larger piece of the receiving pie. Fantasy managers should keep a close eye on his status ahead of Sunday and have plans in place should he not clear concussion protocol.

metadata.title: Ja'Marr Chase - Questionable for Sunday
metadata.description: Chase remains in concussion protocol and will be listed as questionable for Sunday's game at Miami, Charlie Goldsmith reports.
metadata.analysis: Chase is practicing Friday but will still need clearance from an independent neurologist. Fellow Bengals wideout Tee Higgins (adductor) isn't practicing Friday and thus appears in more danger of missing Week 5.

metadata.title: Ja'Marr Chase (concussion) in uniform at practice Friday
metadata.description: Ja'Marr Chase is in uniform at practice on Friday.
metadata.analysis: Chase was officially limited at practice on Thursday. He'll have till Saturday to clear concussion protocol in time for Sunday's game.

metadata.title: Ja'Marr Chase - At practice Friday
metadata.description: Chase (concussion) is in uniform for Friday's practice, Charlie Goldsmith of Fox 19 Now Cincinnati reports.
metadata.analysis: Chase remains in the league's concussion protocol, and while it's a good sign he's on the field for Friday's practice, it doesn't yet mean he's cleared all the necessary steps to play Sunday against the Dolphins. The Bengals will release official injury designations later Friday, and fantasy managers will then have a better idea of the star wideout's availability for Week 5.

metadata.title: Ja'Marr Chase Will be Questionable for Week 5
metadata.description: Cincinnati Bengals head coach Zac Taylor said that star wide receiver Ja'Marr Chase (concussion) is still in the league's concussion protocol, according to Paul Dehner Jr. of The Athletic. Chase was able to practice again on Friday, but he will be listed as questionable to play on Sunday in Week 5 against the Miami Dolphins. It does not make fantasy managers' decisions any easier this weekend, and the 26-year-old All-Pro pass-catcher could end up being a true game-time decision on Sunday morning. Hopefully, we will have some clarification on his status by Saturday night. With fellow wideout Tee Higgins (groin) also questionable to play, the Bengals could be without their top two pass-catchers on the road against the winless Dolphins. Chase already has 21 catches for 212 yards and three touchdowns in the first four games of the season and will be a must-start in fantasy lineups if he is cleared from the concussion protocol by Sunday. Tight end Mike Gesicki's weekly value is trending up with both Chase and Higgins up in the air to play.

metadata.title: Ja'Marr Chase (concussion) officially limited Thursday
metadata.description: Ja'Marr Chase (concussion) was officially limited at practice on Thursday.
metadata.analysis: The star wideout was able to return to practice as a limited participant on Thursday. That's a big step in the right direction, and it gives him a real chance to clear the NFL's concussion protocols in time for Sunday's game against the Dolphins. Fantasy managers should have no hesitations starting him if he's active this week.

metadata.title: Ja'Marr Chase - Officially limited Thursday
metadata.description: Chase (concussion) was officially listed as a limited participant at Thursday's practice, Ben Baby of ESPN.com reports.
metadata.analysis: Chase took a step in the right direction Thursday after being unable to practice Wednesday. In order to have a chance to clear the league's five-step concussion protocol in time to suit up Sunday against the Dolphins, Chase would need to practice without limitations Friday. He was diagnosed with a concussion after exiting this past Sunday's loss to the Jaguars in the first half.

metadata.title: Ja'Marr Chase (concussion) practicing Thursday
metadata.description: Ja'Marr Chase was wearing pads during practice on Thursday.
metadata.analysis: Chase remains in concussion protocol, but it is a step in the right direction for him. He will need to be monitored in practice again on Friday.

metadata.title: Ja'Marr Chase - Returns to practice Thursday
metadata.description: Chase (concussion) was present for the media-access portion of Thursday's practice, Ben Baby of ESPN.com reports.
metadata.analysis: In the wake of his rough exit from this past Sunday's game against the Jaguars, Chase has been embedded in the concussion protocol and sat out Wednesday's session, but his return one day later indicates he's making some progress through it. Thursday's injury report will reveal his activity level, as well as that of fellow WR Tee Higgins (groin/neck).

metadata.title: Ja'Marr Chase Back at Practice as he Works Through Concussion Protocol
metadata.description: Cincinnati Bengals star wide receiver Ja'Marr Chase (head) is back at practice on Thursday as he continues to work his way through the league's concussion protocol, according to Ben Baby of ESPN. Chase suffered a concussion in the Week 4 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars and did not practice on Wednesday. His status for this weekend's game in Miami against the Dolphins is still up in the air, but his return to practice on Thursday at least gives him a chance to clear the NFL's concussion protocol by the weekend. Fellow wideout Tee Higgins (groin) is also on the Week 5 injury report and did not practice on Wednesday, so Cincy's receiving corps is banged up right now. Chase is a must-start in all traditional fantasy football leagues when he is active, but his status for Week 5 could be a game-time decision on Sunday. The five-time Pro Bowler has caught 21 of his 28 targets for 212 yards and three touchdowns through his first four games in 2026. Fantasy managers will want to check back on Chase's status for Friday's final injury report. UPDATE: Chase was officially limited in his return to practice, and he remains in the league's concussion protocol.

metadata.title: Ja'Marr Chase (concussion) not practicing Wednesday
metadata.description: Ja'Marr Chase missed practice on Wednesday.
metadata.analysis: Chase remains unlikely to play in Week 5 as he is in the concussion protocol.

metadata.title: Ja'Marr Chase - Remains in concussion protocol
metadata.description: Chase remains in the league's concussion protocol Wednesday, Ben Baby of ESPN.com reports.
metadata.analysis: Chase suffered a concussion early in last Sunday's loss to the Jaguars and isn't certain to be cleared in time for Week 5 against the Dolphins. The Bengals then have a Week 6 bye, so it's possible Chase won't play again for another couple weeks. Dohnte Meyers and Mike Gesicki would be in line for increased target shares if Chase is unable to play versus Miami. It's also notable that Tee Higgins (groin) was limited in Wednesday's practice.

metadata.title: Ja'Marr Chase remains in concussion protocol
metadata.description: Bengals WR Ja'Marr Chase remains in concussion protocol.
metadata.analysis: Chase remains day-to-day. He is likely to sit in Week 5 unless he can clear all protocols by Friday.

metadata.title: Ja'Marr Chase Working Through the Concussion Protocol
metadata.description: Cincinnati Bengals head coach Zac Taylor said that star wide receiver Ja'Marr Chase (head) is working through the league's concussion protocol, according to Paul Dehner Jr. of The Athletic. It is unclear what that means as far as Chase's practice status on Wednesday, but he is still in play to potentially suit up in Week 5 on Sunday at the Miami Dolphins. Fellow wideout Tee Higgins (groin) is also dealing with an injury, but he was limited on Wednesday and should have a pretty good chance of playing this weekend. We will continue to keep a close eye on Chase's participation throughout the week, but for now, fantasy managers should consider him very questionable to face Miami in South Beach on Sunday. With Cincy's bye coming in Week 6, it is very possible that the Bengals play it safe and give Chase two full weeks to heal up. If he does not play against the Dolphins, then receiver Dohnte Meyers and tight end Mike Gesicki will become very interesting fantasy options this week in an excellent matchup against the winless Dolphins. Chase is a must-start in fantasy anytime he is active. He has 21 catches for 212 yards and three touchdowns through four games in 2026.

metadata.title: Mitchell Tinsley A Waiver Pickup Consideration After Ja'Marr Chase Injury
metadata.description: Cincinnati Bengals wide receiver Mitchell Tinsley saw his first regular season action in Week 4 due to WR Ja'Marr Chase (head) suffering a concussion and being forced to exit the contest. Tinsley caught three of his seven targets for 49 yards in a game that also saw Bengals WR2 Tee Higgins (adductor) get hurt. Tinsley could be the WR2 for the Bengals in Week 5 and see plenty of volume in a high-powered passing offense. It's unclear if Chase or Higgins will miss Week 5, but we won't know their status until much closer to the game. In deeper leagues, a chance to get a team's WR2 off waivers, even if they're not considered very talented, is one that shouldn't be passed up on. Cincinnati's quarterback, Joe Burrow, is capable of feeding a high volume of accurate targets to whoever he throws to. A matchup with the struggling Miami Dolphins next week could present the perfect opportunity for Tinsley to have a career game, especially if Higgins plays at less than 100 percent due to his injury. In leagues with 14 or more teams, he should be a priority pickup as a spot starter, even if it's only for one week. Cincinnati's second leading receiver last game was WR Dohnte Myers, who was targeted nine times. Both are good players to add off waivers, as Burrow is more than capable of fueling huge games for multiple of his pass-catchers.

metadata.title: Ja'Marr Chase (concussion) in protocol, labeled day-to-day
metadata.description: Ja'Marr Chase is going through the league's concussion protocol.
metadata.analysis: Chase will need to clear the protocol before having a chance to play Sunday in Miami, but it is a positive sign that head coach Zac Taylor said Monday that the star wideout is day-to-day. Chase was knocked out of Week 4's loss to the Jaguars early, leaving plenty of extra targets for Tee Higgins and the rest of the Bengals' route runners.

metadata.title: Ja'Marr Chase Remains in Concussion Protocol
metadata.description: Cincinnati Bengals wide receiver Ja'Marr Chase (concussion) remains in the league's concussion protocol after leaving Sunday's loss to Jacksonville. Head coach Zac Taylor told Jay Morrison on Monday that Chase is considered day to day, but there is still no timetable for his return. Chase was injured in the second quarter after taking a hard hit following a reception and did not return, finishing with three catches for 27 yards. He now has 21 receptions for 212 yards and three touchdowns through four games. Cincinnati visits Miami in Week 5, but Chase will need to clear the protocol before he can play. His status should become clearer once the Bengals return to practice later this week.

metadata.title: Ja'Marr Chase (concussion) ruled out
metadata.description: The Bengals have ruled out WR Ja'Marr Chase for the remainder of Week 4 with a concussion.
metadata.analysis: Chase was injured on a facemask penalty in the first half and will not return. He caught all three of his targets for 27 yards prior to the injury. Tee Higgins and Dohnte Meyers will serve as the primary wide receivers for the remainder of the game.

metadata.title: Ja'Marr Chase - Won't return vs. Jacksonville
metadata.description: Chase (concussion) has been ruled out for the rest of Sunday's game against the Jaguars.
metadata.analysis: Chase was taken out of the game to be checked for a possible concussion after his facemask was pulled at the end of a four-yard catch in the second quarter. With the superstar wide receiver done for the day, Tee Higgins will be Joe Burrow's top target in the passing game, with Dohnte Meyers, Mitchell Tinsley, running back Chase Brown and tight end Mike Gesicki all in line for bigger roles for the rest of the game. Chase will need to clear the league's five-step concussion protocol in order to be available for Week 5 against the Dolphins on Sunday, Oct. 11.

metadata.title: Ja'Marr Chase headed to the locker room
metadata.description: Bengals WR Ja'Marr Chase is headed to the locker room. He is now being evaluated for a concussion and is questionable to return.
metadata.analysis: Chase suffered an apparent injury on the Bengals' last possession after a face mask penalty by a Jaguars' defender. The Bengals will turn to Tee Higgins as the primary pass catcher if Chase cannot return.

metadata.title: Ja'Marr Chase - Being evaluated for possible concussion
metadata.description: Chase is under evaluation for a possible concussion during Sunday's game versus the Jaguars.
metadata.analysis: Chase was ripped down by his facemask on a four-yard catch by a Jacksonville defender in the second quarter and remained on the turf before hitting the sidelines and eventually going to the locker room. If he ends up entering the protocol for head injuries, he'll be out for the rest of Week 4, and Tee Higgins, Dohnte Meyers and Mitchell Tinsley will be tasked with WR duties for the rest of Sunday.

metadata.title: Ja'Marr Chase Ruled Out With Concussion
metadata.description: Cincinnati Bengals wide receiver Ja'Marr Chase (concussion) has been ruled out for the rest of Sunday's game against the Jacksonville Jaguars, according to Paul Dehner. Chase was injured in the second quarter after being brought down by his facemask, with his head hitting the turf on the play. He was able to walk off under his own power before going to the medical tent and later the locker room. Chase caught all three of his targets for 26 yards before leaving. He will now enter the league's concussion protocol, putting his status for Week 5 in question.

metadata.title: Ja'Marr Chase Being Evaluated for Concussion, Questionable to Return
metadata.description: Cincinnati Bengals wide receiver Ja'Marr Chase (concussion) is being evaluated for a concussion and is questionable to return, according to the team. He was seen entering the blue medical tent in a Week 4 matchup with the Jacksonville Jaguars, according to Charlie Goldsmith of the Charlie's Chalkboard newsletter and FOX19. The injury occurred after Chase caught a four-yard pass and Jacksonville cornerback Jarrian Jones was called for a face mask penalty. Other wide receivers for the Bengals include Tee Higgins, Dohnte Meyers and Mitch Tinsley.

metadata.title: Ja'Marr Chase excellent in Week 3 loss
metadata.description: Ja'Marr Chase caught 9-of-12 targets for 98 yards and a touchdown in a 30-27 loss to the Steelers.
metadata.analysis: Chase led the team in all of the receiving categories for the Bengals Sunday. Chase and Joe Burrow connected on a three-yard touchdown strike in the first quarter. Chase and the Bengals will take on the Jaguars in Week 4.

metadata.title: Ja'Marr Chase has Another Big Game in Divisional Loss
metadata.description: Cincinnati Bengals wide receiver Ja'Marr Chase was once again the team's leading receiver in the 30-27 Week 3 loss on the road to the division-rival Pittsburgh Steelers, catching nine of his 12 targets for 98 yards and a touchdown. It was a slow start to the season for Chase, as he caught just two passes for 12 yards in the season-opening win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. But he had seven catches on nine targets for 75 yards and his first two touchdowns of the year in the Week 2 victory over the Houston Texans. That is now three touchdowns in the last two games for Chase, who is an absolute must-start each and every week. Chase's nine catches were three more than Tee Higgins, and his 12 targets were five more than Higgins. The 26-year-old All-Pro will have a strong chance to make it three straight weeks with a trip to the end zone when the Bengals face off against the Jacksonville Jaguars next Sunday in Week 4.

metadata.title: Ja'Marr Chase - Busy afternoon in loss
metadata.description: Chase brought in nine of 12 targets for 98 yards and a touchdown in the Bengals' 30-27 loss to the Steelers on Sunday.
metadata.analysis: Chase paced the Bengals in receptions, receiving yards and targets, taking his customary position at the top of the team's pass-catching corps. The All-Pro wideout recorded his touchdown on a three-yard grab with just under six minutes remaining in the first quarter to answer a Steelers opening-drive score, marking his third trip to the end zone already this season. Chase will aim to stay just as productive when the Jaguars pay a visit for a Week 4 showdown next Sunday.

metadata.title: Ja'Marr Chase Ready For Another Huge Performance In Pittsburgh
metadata.description: Cincinnati Bengals wide receiver Ja'Marr Chase will face the Pittsburgh Steelers on the road in Week 3. Chase shook off a lackluster Week 1 performance with a strong stat line against the Houston Texans last week. The superstar wideout caught seven passes for 75 yards and two touchdowns in the 20-6 win in Week 2. Despite putting up WR1 numbers last game, Chase still has not reached 100 receiving yards this season. Chase will likely change that on Sunday against the Steelers. The Pittsburgh defense has been stingy against the pass this season, allowing the sixth-fewest passing yards, but Chase is no ordinary receiver. Chase is arguably the best wide receiver in football with a quarterback that isn't afraid to throw him the ball in any situation. That is a dangerous combination for opposing defenses to face because they can break off a big play at any moment. Chase is ranked WR3 in our RotoBaller Week 3 PPR rankings, making him a top-tier WR1 heading into the weekend. Fantasy managers should never question having him in their starting lineups for as long as he's healthy.

metadata.title: Ja'Marr Chase hauls in two touchdowns Sunday
metadata.description: Ja'Marr Chase caught 7-of-9 targets for 75 yards and two touchdowns in the Bengals 20-6 win over the Texans on Sunday.
metadata.analysis: Chase recorded both of the touchdowns scored by Cincinnati on Sunday, including an incredible catch where he just barely got both feet in. He remains a locked and loaded WR1 heading into next week against the Steelers.

metadata.title: Ja'Marr Chase - First pair of TDs in win
metadata.description: Chase brought in seven of nine targets for 75 yards and two touchdowns in the Bengals' 20-6 win over the Texans on Sunday.
metadata.analysis: Chase recorded what already profiles as a Catch of the Year candidate on the first of his two touchdowns, one that saw him exhibit elite body control while making a narrowly inbounds, spinning grab from 32 yards out late in the second quarter. He went on to add an 18-yard TD reception in the latter portion of the third quarter as well, and he finished with the team lead in receptions while checking in as the runner-up to Tee Higgins in both receiving yards and targets. The rewarding fantasy day atoned for a quiet two-reception and scoreless Week 1 for the perennial Pro Bowler, who'll next tangle with the Steelers defense in a Week 3 road matchup next Sunday.

metadata.title: Ja'Marr Chase Scores Twice In Week 2 Win
metadata.description: Cincinnati Bengals wide receiver Ja'Marr Chase bounced back in a big way in Week 2 with seven catches for 75 yards and two scores in the 20-6 win over the Houston Texans. Chase shook off that disappointing season opener performance as he and quarterback Joe Burrow connected often throughout the contest. The star wideout finished first on the team in receptions, but trailed teammate Tee Higgins in receiving yards and targets. This game gave fantasy managers a much-needed sigh of relief and should give them confidence about starting Chase heading into a Week 3 matchup against the Pittsburgh Steelers. The Steelers have allowed 20 points to opposing teams in each of their first two games, which bodes well for the Bengals' chances of scoring. Chase is the focal point of the Cincinnati passing attack, so when the offense succeeds, he's usually the reason why. Chase is one of the most reliable targets in the league, and he should be considered a top-end WR1 heading into Week 3.

metadata.title: Ja'Marr Chase Ready To Bounce Back Against Houston
metadata.description: Cincinnati Bengals wide receiver Ja'Marr Chase will face the Houston Texans in Week 2. Chase had an underwhelming performance in the Bengals season opener, catching two passes for just 12 yards in the team's 33-27 victory over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. The superstar receiver was basically a non-factor in a game where Cincinnati scored over 30 points, so fantasy managers are likely disappointed in their early first-round pick. Chase will have the opportunity to bounce back in a big way against a Texans defense that just allowed 36 points to Josh Allen and the Buffalo Bills in Week 1. Chase was listed on the injury report in Week 1 but was absent from the report in Week 2, signaling that he's put any injury issues to rest heading into the weekend. Chase is ranked WR6 in our RotoBaller Week 2 PPR rankings, making him a strong start. Another piece of news to mention is that quarterback Joe Burrow has been dealing with back tightness all week and is listed as questionable for Sunday's matchup. His questionable tag is concerning, but Burrow practiced fully on Friday so all signs point to him playing this week. Despite his troubling Week 1 performance and quarterback questions, fantasy managers should feel confident starting Chase as their WR1 once again in Week 2.

metadata.title: Ja'Marr Chase - Not worried about knee
metadata.description: Chase said Thursday that his knee feels great, Kelsey Conway of the Cincinnati Enquirer reports.
metadata.analysis: Chase sustained a knee injury in practice Aug. 25 but hasn't seemed bothered by it recently, as he suited up for the Week 1 win over the Buccaneers and has been practicing without limitations ahead of Sunday's road matchup with Houston. The star wide receiver had a disappointing 12 receiving yards against the Buccaneers, but starting slow has become the norm for Chase, who had 39, 62 and 26 receiving yards in the preceding three season openers. He bounced back from his 26-yard Week 1 showing in 2025 with 165 yards and a touchdown in Week 2.

metadata.title: Ja'Marr Chase Says his Knee Feels Great
metadata.description: Cincinnati Bengals wide receiver Ja'Marr Chase told The Cincinnati Enquirer's Kelsey Conway on Thursday that his knee feels great. Chase hyperextended his knee in a training camp practice on Aug. 25 and was on the injury report heading into the season opener, but he was active in the Week 1 victory over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. The 26-year-old five-time Pro Bowler and two-time first-team All-Pro played 94% of the offensive snaps last Sunday, but he caught only two passes on four targets for 12 yards in a bust performance for the No. 1 WR off the board in most fantasy football drafts. Fantasy managers might have been wondering if Chase's knee was to blame. The former fifth overall pick from LSU says his knee is fine, though, so he should be expected to have a much better performance in Week 2 on the road against the Houston Texans. It is even better news that Chase has not been on the Bengals' injury report at all heading into this weekend. Start him with confidence.

metadata.title: Ja'Marr Chase very quiet to open season
metadata.description: Ja'Marr Chase caught 2-of-4 targets for 12 yards in the Bengals 33-27 win over the Buccaneers.
metadata.analysis: It was a Week 1 to forget for Chase fantasy managers to say the least. There shouldn't be too much of concern after one week, though he draws an even tougher matchup in Week 2 against the Texans.

metadata.title: Ja'Marr Chase - Quiet start to season
metadata.description: Chase brought in two of four targets for 12 yards in the Bengals' 33-27 win over the Buccaneers on Sunday.
metadata.analysis: Despite the Bengals shaking off their usual Week 1 offensive doldrums, it was still a relatively modest day for the air attack. Joe Burrow threw for a respectable 254 yards, but Chase wasn't prioritized anywhere near the norm and actually finished behind all of Mike Gesicki, Tee Higgins and Chase Brown in targets. Chase will continue to be the focal point of opposing defenses every week, but he should be in line for more opportunity in a Week 2 road matchup against a Texans defense that was surprisingly gashed by the Bills on Sunday.

metadata.title: Ja'Marr Chase Disappoints In Week 1 Win
metadata.description: Cincinnati Bengals wide receiver Ja'Marr Chase had two catches for 12 yards on four targets in the 33-27 win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Chase was uncharacteristically uninvolved in the offense and the Bengals still managed to snag a win. Chase was the fourth-most targeted Bengal, trailing Mike Gesicki, Tee Higgins, and Chase Brown. It may be relevant to note that despite not entering the game with an injury designation, Chase was listed DNP in Friday's practice. It remains to be seen if the knee issue had anything to do with his abnormal performance in Week 1. If all is well, Chase should be considered a massive bounce-back candidate for Week 2 against the Houston Texans. The Texans were one of the best defenses in the NFL last season, but the Buffalo Bills were able to drop 36 points against them in Week 1, so Cincinnati may be able to do the same. Chase should still be considered a must-start WR1 heading into Week 2, despite the disappointing season debut.

metadata.title: Ja'Marr Chase - Good to go, no designation
metadata.description: Chase (knee) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game against Tampa Bay.
metadata.analysis: Chase was a full practice participant Wednesday and Thursday before resting Friday, with the Bengals citing 'rest' rather than his knee as the reason for Friday's absence. He suffered a minor knee hyperextension Aug. 25 and returned to practice within two weeks. Chase should be ready for his usual role this Sunday against the Buccaneers.
